newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital to have 226,000 unemployed in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China capital to have 226,000 unemployed in 1997.

text.p: China's capital Beijing will be able to find jobs for just 200,000 of the 426,000 people expected to be looking for work in 1997, the China Economic Times on Thursday quoted an employment conference as concluding.

At least 175,000 new workers would enter the city's labour pool in 1997 while another 251,000 would be seeking jobs after being laid off or leaving former posts, it quoted officials at the conference as saying.
"The supply and demand problem in the Beijing labour market will be very pronounced this year," it said.
Many of the surplus workers in Beijing -- which has a population of around 11 million -- were expected to come from factories forced to close down or reduce output, it said.

Some 380 plants had closed or slashed output in 1996, a rise of 23.7 percent from the year before, it said. Payrolls at such factories were cut by 124,000 people last year, up 17.8 percent from 1995, it said.

The Chinese government, fearing social unrest resulting from mass unemployment, requires state-owned enterprises to provide stipends and health care to employees even if production lines are standing idle, but standards of support vary.
